# payments

Install: `composer require rasuvaeff/payments`

Rules: namespace `Rasuvaeff\Payments`. Money is integer minor units — never
floats. `PaymentIntent` is application-owned; `PaymentAttempt`/`RefundAttempt`
are single provider executions. `PaymentState::canTransitionTo()` is advisory
only — never use it to discard an accepted webhook observation.
`ObservedPaymentEvent` is a sanitized observation, not authoritative state;
re-fetch authoritative provider state before changing a projection. Inject
PSR-18/PSR-17 implementations; keep retries and timeouts outside the transport;
never serialize or log `AuthContext` credentials. Validate a webhook before
atomically claiming its provider event id. Never persist raw body or validation
headers. Validation regexes anchor with `\z`, not `$`. `CreatePaymentRequest`
takes an optional `paymentMethod`: omit it for the deferred flow where the
customer picks a method client-side. Mount the webhook route before any
body-parsing middleware — a consumed stream reads back empty and fails every
signature check (reported as the `empty_body` outcome).

Contracts API:

```php
$money = Money::minorUnits(1_200, 'EUR');   // non-negative int + /^[A-Z]{3}\z/ currency
$money->add($m); $money->subtract($m);      // same currency; overflow/negative => throw
$money->equals($other);                     // amount AND currency — use for order reconciliation
$money->isGreaterThan($other); $money->isLessThan($other); // same currency required
$money->multiply(3, 100);                   // integer numerator/denominator, half-up rounding
$money->isZero();

$provider = new PaymentProvider('stripe');  // /^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\z/
$opId = new OperationId('op-1');            // app-issued command id, <=255 bytes
$payment = new PaymentReference(provider: $provider, id: 'pi_1', kind: 'payment');
$refund = new RefundReference(provider: $provider, id: 're_1');
$customer = new CustomerReference(id: 'cus-app', providerId: 'cus_1');
$method = new PaymentMethodReference(id: 'pm_1', kind: 'card');
```

- Enums: `PaymentState` (Pending, RequiresPaymentMethod, RequiresAction, RequiresCapture, Processing, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled; `canTransitionTo(self): bool` advisory, terminal states return false). `Succeeded`/`Failed`/`Canceled` are terminal, so a recoverable provider status must never map to them — Stripe's `requires_payment_method` maps to `RequiresPaymentMethod` because the same intent can still reach `succeeded`, `RefundState` (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Canceled), `CaptureMethod`/`ConfirmationMethod` (Automatic, Manual).
- `PaymentAttempt(operationId, provider, payment, amount, state, rawStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, requestInfo, ?failure, ?nextAction)`: one provider execution; reference provider must match, `updatedAt >= createdAt`.
- `RefundAttempt(operationId, provider, refund, payment, requestedAmount, ?actualAmount, state, rawStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, requestInfo, ?failure)`.
- `PaymentIntent(id, amount, createdAt, attempts)`: application aggregate; attempt currencies must match intent currency.
- `PaymentFailure(code, ?message, retryable = false, details = [])`: sanitized, scalar details only.
- `ProviderRequestInfo(receivedAt, ?requestId, ?rateLimitRemaining, ?retryAfterSeconds)`: allow-listed response diagnostics.
- `NextAction` (open, `type(): string`): `RedirectToUrl($httpsUrl)`, `UseSdk($sdkName, $scalarPayload)`, `DisplayInstructions($instructionType, $text, $scalarMetadata)`.

Gateway contracts (ISP — optional operations are separate interfaces):

```php
interface PaymentGatewayInterface {
    public function provider(): PaymentProvider;
    public function capabilities(): CapabilitySet;
    public function createPayment(CreatePaymentRequest $request): PaymentAttempt;
    public function retrievePayment(RetrievePaymentRequest $request): PaymentAttempt;
}
// CaptureGatewayInterface::capturePayment(CapturePaymentRequest): PaymentAttempt
// ConfirmGatewayInterface::confirmPayment(PaymentOperationRequest): PaymentAttempt
// CancelGatewayInterface::cancelPayment(PaymentOperationRequest): PaymentAttempt
// RefundGatewayInterface::createRefund(CreateRefundRequest): RefundAttempt
//                        ::retrieveRefund(RetrieveRefundRequest): RefundAttempt
```

- Requests: `CreatePaymentRequest(operationId, amount, paymentMethod, ?customer, captureMethod, confirmationMethod, ?description, metadata, ?idempotencyKey)`, `CapturePaymentRequest(operationId, payment, ?amount, ?idempotencyKey)`, `CreateRefundRequest(operationId, payment, ?amount, ?reason, ?idempotencyKey)`, `PaymentOperationRequest(operationId, payment, ?idempotencyKey)` for confirm/cancel, `RetrievePaymentRequest(operationId, payment)`, `RetrieveRefundRequest(operationId, refund)`.
- Capabilities: `CapabilitySet::of(Capability ...)` (duplicate types rejected), `->get(Class::class): ?T`, `->has(Class::class): bool`, `->all(): list<Capability>`. Shipped: `PartialRefundCapability(?maximumRefunds)`, `SandboxCapability(environment = 'sandbox')`, `ThreeDsCapability(versions)`, `WebhookCapability(signatureRequired = true)`. Implement the `Capability` marker for custom ones.

Registry and router:

```php
$registry = new GatewayRegistry([$gatewayA, $gatewayB]); // duplicate provider => InvalidArgumentException
$registry->get($provider);       // OutOfBoundsException when missing
$registry->has($provider); $registry->providers(); $registry->all();
$registry->capability($provider, ThreeDsCapability::class); // ?ThreeDsCapability

$router = new PaymentGatewayRouter(
    registry: $registry,
    selectionPolicy: new FixedGatewaySelectionPolicy($provider), // or app-owned GatewaySelectionPolicyInterface
);
$attempt = $router->createPayment(new GatewaySelectionContext(request: $create, tenantId: 't1', riskLevel: 'low'));
$router->retrievePayment($retrieve);   // routes by $request->payment->provider
$router->capturePayment($capture);     // LogicException if gateway lacks CaptureGatewayInterface
$router->confirmPayment($op); $router->cancelPayment($op);
$router->createRefund($refundReq); $router->retrieveRefund($retrieveRefund);
```

The policy selects a provider only for creation; existing references route by
their embedded provider. No implicit default policy is shipped.

Transport API:

```php
$request = (new JsonRequestBuilder($requestFactory, $streamFactory))
    ->build('POST', $uri, $data, AuthContext::bearer($token));
$payload = (new JsonResponseDecoder())->decode((new Psr18Transport($client))->send($request));
```

- `AuthContext::bearer($token)` / `::basic($user, $pass)` / `::fromHeaders($map)` — in-memory only.
- `FormRequestBuilder` encodes scalar-only form bodies.
- `JsonResponseDecoder` maps: 401 `UnauthorizedException`, 403 `ForbiddenException`, 404 `NotFoundException`, 429 `RateLimitedException`, 5xx `ServerException`, refund errors `RefundFailedException`, card/decline `ProviderDeclinedException`, other non-2xx `PaymentException`, non-object JSON `MalformedResponseException`. PSR-18 failures become `TransportException`. `PaymentException` carries `providerCode`, `providerType`, `providerParameter`, scalar `details`.

Webhook API:

- `RawJsonRequestBuilderInterface::buildRawJson(method, uri, body, auth)`: implemented by `JsonRequestBuilder`; sends an already-encoded JSON body byte for byte (throws on an empty body). Required when forwarding a document signed elsewhere — a decode/re-encode round trip escapes non-ASCII, turns `{}` into `[]` and drops a trailing zero, so the forwarded document stops being the received one.
- `WebhookInput`: exact `rawBody`, provider, normalized headers and request metadata; use only sanitized accessors for audit data. `header()` requires a non-empty name.
- `WebhookValidatorInterface::validate()`: native union return type `ValidWebhook|InvalidWebhook`. PHP rejects a widened signature and any other returned class, so the two outcomes are the whole contract.
- `WebhookEventTypeExtractorInterface`: extracts the provider's raw event name after validation.
- `WebhookEventRecognizerInterface`: maps a raw name to provider-neutral `ProviderEventType` or returns `null`.
- `WebhookPayloadMapperInterface`: produces sanitized `ObservedPaymentEvent`; throw `UnsupportedWebhookEventException` for a known unsupported payload, `MalformedResponseException` for a payload that can never be mapped. Both are terminal — the claim is completed, not released — because redelivery yields the same verdict and a retry storm gets the endpoint disabled.
- `ObservedPaymentEvent(providerEventId, type, payment, state, rawStatus, occurredAt, ?refund, payload)`: scalar allow-listed payload; refund reference required for `RefundState` and forbidden for `PaymentState`; all references must share one provider.
- `WebhookEventStoreInterface`: atomic `claim(provider, eventId)` returning `?WebhookClaimToken` (null = replayed), `complete(provider, eventId, token)` when the event is durably accepted, `release(provider, eventId, token)` for retryable failures. `complete()` is what makes stale-claim recovery safe: a claim that was never completed and whose lease expired must be reclaimable, a completed one never. Without it a crash between claim and acceptance is answered with a replay outcome (204) forever and the event is lost silently. The token is the fence: both finalisers compare it against the stored claim and are no-ops on a mismatch, so a worker whose lease was taken over cannot complete the new owner's attempt or delete its live claim. Alternative for a same-database queue: commit the claim row and the queue row in one transaction.
- `WebhookClaimToken`: opaque fencing token; `::generate()` gives 128 bits of entropy, `equals()` compares values in constant time, value is a non-empty URL-safe string of at most 128 bytes.
- `QueuedWebhookEventAcceptance($queue)`: durable phase-one queue, policy `AfterValidation`.
- `SynchronousWebhookEventAcceptance($reconciler)`: synchronous authoritative reconciliation, policy `AfterPersistence`.
- `WebhookProcessingResult` is an open interface; `WebhookProcessor::process()` narrows to these six, a decorating processor may add its own:
  - `ProcessedWebhook`: `$event` (`ObservedPaymentEvent`), `$acknowledgementPolicy`.
  - `WebhookValidationFailed`: `$reason`.
  - `UnknownWebhookEvent`: `$providerEventId`, `$providerEventType` (nullable).
  - `UnsupportedWebhookEvent`: `$providerEventId`, `$type`, `$reason`.
  - `RejectedWebhookEvent`: `$providerEventId`, `$reason`, `$type` (nullable) — validated event whose payload can never be mapped.
  - `ReplayedWebhookEvent`: `$providerEventId`.

```php
$processor = new WebhookProcessor(
    validator: $validator,
    eventTypeExtractor: $extractor,
    eventRecognizer: $recognizer,
    payloadMapper: $mapper,
    eventStore: $eventStore,
    eventAcceptance: new QueuedWebhookEventAcceptance($queue),
);
$result = $processor->process(new WebhookInput($rawBody, $provider, $headers));

if ($result instanceof ProcessedWebhook) {
    $policy = $result->acknowledgementPolicy;
    $event = $result->event;
}
```

The queue must be idempotent by provider and event id. `ProcessedWebhook` is
returned only after the configured durable boundary succeeds; retryable failures
release the claim and propagate so the HTTP bridge can return a retryable
non-success response. Every returned outcome — including the ignoring ones —
completes the claim.

Webhook HTTP endpoint:

```php
$registry = new WebhookProcessorRegistry([
    new WebhookProcessorRegistration(provider: $provider, processor: $processor),
]); // duplicate provider => InvalidArgumentException
$controller = new WebhookController(registry: $registry, responseFactory: $psr17ResponseFactory, logger: $psr3Logger); // logger optional
$response = $controller->handle($serverRequest, 'stripe'); // PSR-7
```

`WebhookController` responses carry only a status and an
`X-Payments-Webhook-Outcome` header, never payloads or validation reasons:
404 `provider_not_found`; 204 `processed`/`replayed`/`ignored_unknown`/`ignored_unsupported`/`rejected_payload`;
400 `validation_failed`, 400 `empty_body`; 503 `processing_failed` on exception (retryable);
500 `processing_failed` for a foreign result type.
